title: What If You Stood on the Surface of Venus?

scenes.text: What if you stood on Venus? The first thing you'd feel isn't the heat.
It's the air itself. About ninety times Earth's pressure, like standing nine hundred meters deep in the ocean.
Then the heat: about 457 degrees Celsius, a temperature at which lead is a liquid. Lead melts at 327.
Humans would last seconds. Even machines struggle, and most landers died within an hour.
The Soviet lander Venera 13 was built to last about half an hour. It kept working for 127 minutes.
It sent back fourteen color photos before going silent in 1982. Nothing has lasted longer there since.
